## Claim check (abstract hypotheses; rules fixed in scripts/render_summary.py)

| Claim | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Physics-constrained diffusion is sharper than the deterministic baseline (closer to observed sharpness) | **supported** | grad ratio 1.46 vs 0.69; HF ratio 1.26 vs 0.71 (1 = observed) |
| Physics-constrained diffusion is sharper than unconstrained diffusion (closer to observed sharpness) | **not supported** | grad ratio 1.46 vs 1.40; HF ratio 1.26 vs 1.05 (1 = observed) |
| Physics constraints make forecasts more physically consistent | **supported** | envelope / monotone violation fraction diff_phys+G+P 0.032 / 0.034, diff_phys 0.034 / 0.033, diff_plain 0.053 / 0.085, det 0.015 / 0.215; monotone violations are scored with the same stress perturbation used in the training loss (in-sample for the physics models); observations themselves: envelope 0.035, rate 0.022 (fewer violations than observed = over-constraint, not physics) |
| Physics-constrained diffusion is more accurate (CRPS) than the baselines | **partly supported** | vs clim_anomaly: diff -0.0753 [-0.0986, -0.0566]; vs climatology: diff -0.0417 [-0.0638, -0.0246]; vs det: diff -0.0209 [-0.0247, -0.0163]; vs diff_plain: diff 0.0030 [0.0008, 0.0058]; vs persistence: diff -0.0511 [-0.0657, -0.0376] (negative = proposed better); MAE: vs climatology: -0.0099 [-0.0273, 0.0039]; vs det: 0.0109 [0.0052, 0.0183]; vs diff_plain: 0.0044 [0.0009, 0.0085]; vs persistence: -0.0193 [-0.0302, -0.0078]. CRPS of a single deterministic forecast equals its MAE, so CRPS gains over point baselines partly reflect being an ensemble; physics constraints cost accuracy relative to unconstrained diffusion where that difference is positive. Source: results/test/paired_tests.csv |
| Ensemble uncertainty is calibrated (uncertainty-aware estimates) | **not supported (overconfident: intervals too narrow)** | 90 % coverage 0.729, 50 % coverage 0.412, spread-skill 0.91 |

## Statistical caveats

- 12 test locations: bootstrap intervals over so few location clusters are likely too narrow; p-values are from 1000 bootstrap draws (0.000 means < 0.001) and are not corrected for multiple comparisons.
- **No conclusion about drought effects is solid yet**: the drought-labelled test sample is far too small (counts above).

Not tested: semi-synthetic oracle (cut by project owner's instruction: no synthetic data). Classifier-free guidance ablation (not run, see PROGRESS.md).

Limitations: see docs/LIMITATIONS.md. The drought effect is a model-based estimate, not ground truth.
